s00-title.text: Your AIO 2 sends a line of numbers every second. Here's how to turn it into a live weather station you can read at a glance.

card.title: Your wind sensor, live
card.subtitle: Wind, weather and logging for the Met One AIO 2.

s01-how.text: The computer wired to the sensor reads it in Chrome or Edge, and saves every reading. Then any phone or computer can watch.

card.title: Sensor, computer, anywhere
card.subtitle: The sensor computer reads the port in Chrome or Edge. Every reading is saved online.
chips: Chrome or Edge on that PC

s02-signin.text: On the sensor computer, open wind sensor dot on forge dot com, and sign in with the station password.
s02-signin.caption: On the sensor computer, open wind-sensor.on-forge.com, and sign in with the station password.

s03-station.text: The first time, name your station, and check its time zone. Today's highs and lows follow it.

s04-output.text: Next, the instrument's output. The factory settings are already filled in. Check they match your sensor, tick the box, and save.

s05-connection.text: This is the Connection page. The port is set to ninety-six hundred baud, the sensor's default. The console only listens. It never changes your sensor's settings.
s05-connection.caption: This is the Connection page. The port is set to 9600 baud, the sensor's default. The console only listens. It never changes your sensor's settings.

s06-connect.text: With the sensor plugged in, click Connect instrument. Chrome shows a list of ports. Pick the one the sensor is on, like COM two.
s06-connect.caption: With the sensor plugged in, click Connect instrument. Chrome shows a list of ports. Pick the one the sensor is on, like COM2.

s07-port.text: Not sure which port? Open Device Manager, and look under Ports. And close any other program using it first, like Comet.

card.title: Device Manager, then Ports
card.subtitle: Unplug the sensor's cable and watch which entry disappears. Only one program can use a port at a time.

s08-demo.text: No sensor connected right now? Start the demo. It's clearly marked, and nothing it shows is saved.

s09-dial.text: This is the wind dial. The arrow points from where the wind is coming from. It glides between readings, and the dots around the edge fade over a minute.

s10-rose.text: Behind it is the wind rose. Each petal shows how often the wind came from that direction, colored by strength. Blue is light air. Red is storm force.

s11-detail.text: On the right, the ten-minute average, the peak reading, and today's peak.
s11-detail.caption: On the right, the 10-minute average, the peak reading, and today's peak.

s12-cards.text: Below, temperature with today's high and low, humidity, and pressure, each with its trend for the last hour.

s13-status.text: The status strip along the top shows what's happening. If the internet drops, readings wait in the browser, and upload on their own.

s14-history.text: History charts any range, up to a month at a time. These readings are simulated for this video. A gap means nothing was saved, so an outage is never hidden.

s15-log.text: The log lists every reading, newest first, with the raw line from the sensor.

s16-export.text: To keep a copy, pick the days, and download a spreadsheet file.

s17-phone.text: On your phone, open the same address and sign in. You'll see the same readings, from anywhere.

s18-outro.text: Leave the browser open on the sensor computer, and keep it awake. It logs every second, for as long as it runs.

card.title: Keep the tab open
card.subtitle: It logs every second while the sensor computer is on and awake.
